places.ad: 1380 Ang Mo Kio Ave 1, Singapore 569930
places.w: One of Singapore's largest heartland parks and a global model for river restoration — under the ABC Waters Programme, a 2.7 km concrete stormwater canal was torn out and rebuilt as a 3 km meandering naturalised Kallang River. A 2017-19 NUS study found the naturalised river lifted the park's biodiversity by 33% (197 animal species, incl. 59 birds and 22 dragonflies).

places.ad: Block 159A, Ang Mo Kio Ave 5 (foot of Ang Mo Kio Town Garden West), Singapore
places.w: Singapore's largest bird-singing and display arena — established 1987 from a 1970s gathering of three AMK zebra-dove keepers, it holds more than a thousand cages on 20-foot poles rigged with pulleys across a space the size of two football fields. A rare surviving fragment of kampong-era culture and a stop on the Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail.

places.n: Ang Mo Kio Town Garden West
places.ad: Ang Mo Kio Avenue 5 / Avenue 6 (opposite Ang Mo Kio Public Library), Singapore
places.w: Completed in 1983 as the HDB's largest town-garden project of its day (~21 ha), built on a hillock with spreading greenery, a lotus pond home to some 19 dragonfly species, and a lookout — a pioneering piece of heartland landscaping and an Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail site. (Note: a section near the pond is affected by LTA's North-South Corridor works.)

places.n: Ang Mo Kio Town Garden East
places.ad: Ang Mo Kio Avenue 3 / Avenue 8 (behind Ang Mo Kio MRT), Singapore
places.w: The eastern counterpart town garden, tucked behind Ang Mo Kio MRT at the junction of Avenues 3 and 8 — a landscaped neighbourhood green with ponds and rest areas serving the surrounding HDB blocks.

places.ad: 30 Venus Drive, Singapore 573858
places.w: A 75-ha nature park opened in 2017 on the AMK/Upper Thomson fringe, a quieter gateway into the Central Catchment. About 4 km of trails — the boardwalked Hanguana Trail over a freshwater swamp forest, the Venus Loop and Drongo Trail — link to MacRitchie and the TreeTop Walk.

places.ad: Central Catchment Nature Reserve (via Venus Drive, off Upper Thomson Road), Singapore
places.w: A 250 m free-standing suspension bridge strung between MacRitchie's two highest points, Bukit Peirce and Bukit Kalang, high in the rainforest canopy — reached on foot from the AMK-side Venus Drive / Windsor trailheads. Closed Mondays (except public holidays).

places.ad: Casuarina Road / Upper Thomson Road, Singapore
places.w: A park around Singapore's second-oldest reservoir (1910s) whose 900 m nature boardwalk, built in 1998 along existing trails, threads one of the island's last mature secondary forests at the water's edge — home to more than 900 flowering plants, 100 ferns and 250 animal species.

places.ad: Upper Thomson Road (near Springleaf), Singapore
places.w: Singapore's 7th nature park (opened 2019), built around the atmospheric ruins of a 1930s-60s Hainanese village and a key conservation site for the critically endangered Raffles' banded langur. Five trails (3.8 km) — Ruins and Figs, Stream and Ferns, Rambutan, Langur and Macaque — wind past old village foundations and troops of long-tailed macaques.

places.ad: Ang Mo Kio Town Centre (trail markers islandwide across AMK), Singapore
places.w: NHB's self-guided trail through Singapore's quintessential heartland town — refreshed in 2023 to 40 heritage sites and 10 markers across three routes (Iconic Landmarks, Hidden Heartland Gems, Scenic Fringes), linking the Clover Block, Kebun Baru Birdsinging Club, Chu Sheng Temple, Church of Christ the King, Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park and more.

places.ad: 2221 Ang Mo Kio Ave 8, Singapore 569809
places.w: The only Catholic church in Ang Mo Kio — its foundation stone laid in 1981 by Archbishop Gregory Yong, it cost around S$3 million (then twice any other church in Singapore) and opened in 1982 before being rebuilt in 2002. Marked on the Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail; the facade carries a statue of Christ the King.

places.ad: 259 Ang Mo Kio Avenue 2, Singapore 560259
places.w: The only block of circular flats the HDB ever built — four round towers joined into a four-leaf-clover plan (completed 1981), part of a late-1970s pilot of seven distinctively designed blocks meant to give estates their own identity. Built in solid brick with round rooms larger than a standard five-room flat; now an AMK icon and a heritage-trail marker.

places.ad: 48 Ang Mo Kio Street 61, Singapore 569163
places.w: A Hokkien-style temple built in 1981 to house three older village temples — Ji Fu Gong, Hua Tang Fu and Long Quan Yan — displaced from Yio Chu Kang's 11th milestone (Ka Tau Au) by redevelopment. Pronounced curved roof ridges mark its Hokkien architecture; former villagers still gather here and it runs community charity. An Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail hidden gem.

places.ad: 5140 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, Singapore 569844
places.w: Ang Mo Kio's HDB-built neighbourhood mosque, opened 21 September 1980 for a community that had earlier prayed at Thomson Road and Kampong Sireh. Part-funded by MUIS with the rest raised by residents through donations and food fairs, it accommodates up to 3,500 worshippers and is a marker on the Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail.

places.ad: Blk 570 Ang Mo Kio Avenue 3, Singapore 560570
places.w: One of the last surviving vintage sand-pit dragon playgrounds in Singapore — a 1980s reproduction of the beloved Toa Payoh design, its dragon head clad in terrazzo mosaic tiles, spine of steel rails, and (uniquely to this one) a mosaic slide. A stop on the Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail's Iconic Landmarks route and a nostalgic icon of heartland childhood.

places.ad: Ang Mo Kio Avenue 1 vicinity, Singapore (Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail; exact street to confirm)
places.w: Established in 1978 and rebuilt in 2011, this joint temple houses three deities' temples displaced when their villages were cleared in the 1970s — Gao Lin Gong, Kim Eang Tong and Leng San Giam. The oldest, Gao Lin Gong, was founded in 1888 by Huang-surname immigrants from Nan An, Fujian, at Kow Tiow Kio ('nine bridges') along today's Ang Mo Kio Avenue 1; its pillars and facade carry carvings handcrafted by artisans in China. An Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail hidden gem.

places.ad: Ang Mo Kio / Yio Chu Kang vicinity (near Lentor Avenue), Singapore (Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail)
places.w: Completed in 1989, this joint temple unites three temples — Sam Ann Fu, Longxuyan Jinshuiguan and the Hong San Chin Huat Temple Association — that once stood at Lak Xun, a village in Yio Chu Kang near present-day Lentor Avenue. One of two new markers added to the refreshed Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail in 2023, recording the town's transformation from plantation land to new town.

places.ad: Ang Mo Kio (Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail hidden gem; exact street to confirm)
places.w: A clan temple and association for people of the Hong (Xiong) surname, first established in 1905 at Buona Vista and relocated over the decades to Ang Mo Kio — a rare surviving surname-clan temple and a Hidden Heartland Gems stop on the Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail, illustrating the village-and-clan networks that predate the new town.

places.n: Old Upper Thomson Road (Thomson Road Grand Prix Circuit)
places.ad: Old Upper Thomson Road (through/around Thomson Nature Park), Singapore
places.w: The surviving loop of the former Thomson Road Grand Prix circuit that hosted the Singapore Grand Prix from 1961 to 1973 — a ~4.8 km course legendary for its danger, with corners nicknamed Devil's Bend, The Snakes and Murder Mile. Now a quiet cycling and walking road on the AMK/Thomson fringe, part of it threading through Thomson Nature Park alongside the old Hainan-village ruins.

places.ad: Teachers' Estate (off Jalan Kuras / Upper Thomson, Yio Chu Kang side), Singapore
places.w: A landed estate developed by the Singapore Teachers' Union — completed 1969 and officially opened in 1971 by then-Education Minister Lim Kim San — whose roads are named after literary figures such as Tu Fu, Rabindranath Tagore and Munshi Abdullah. A Scenic Fringes marker on the Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail.

places.ad: Sembawang Hills Estate (Jalan Leban / Upper Thomson Road vicinity), Singapore
places.w: A private landed estate on the AMK/Upper Thomson fringe, jointly developed in the 1950s by Bukit Sembawang Rubber Estates and Singapore United Rubber Estates as rubber companies pivoted from a declining plantation trade into housing — one of the earliest such estates. A Scenic Fringes marker on the Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail, and home to the well-loved Sembawang Hills Food Centre.

places.n: Ang Mo Kio Fried Kway Teow
places.ad: Ang Mo Kio Central Market & Food Centre, #01-22, Blk 724 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, S560724
places.w: An elderly couple has fried this heritage char kway teow for 40-odd years, opening just 3.5 hours a day — the longest queue in 724 AMK Central, with senior regulars waiting 30 minutes at lunch for smoky, lard-slicked plates.

places.ad: Ang Mo Kio Central Market & Food Centre, #01-01, Blk 724 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, S560724
places.w: Started by the late Haji Yunos Ahmad as a 1965 pushcart at Hastings Road and now run by the third generation, this stall pours a thick, spiced sweet-potato mee rebus gravy that ranks among Singapore's most storied — also known for its satay and soto.

places.ad: Blk 158 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, #01-590 (coffeeshop beside Mayflower Market), S560158
places.w: Two brothers from Kuantan scrape yellowtail by hand daily — fishballs of pure fish, salt and pepper with no flour or filler, tossed Malaysian-style with black sauce and shallot oil. Sells out within four hours; closed Mondays.

places.ad: Ang Mo Kio 628 Market & Food Centre, #01-84, Blk 628 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560628
places.w: AMK's most popular roast-meat stall for two decades, drawing long queues for glossy char siew, shatter-crisp sio bak and a paper-skinned roast duck that fans rate above town shops — the classic combo plate is S$4.50.

places.ad: Blk 232 Ang Mo Kio Ave 3, #01-1222, S560232
places.w: A crab specialist since 1979 (Michelin Plate 2019) whose signature claypot crab bee hoon simmers over 20 crab shells into a rich, sweet milky broth soaked into glass noodles — plus chilli, black pepper and salted-egg crabs. Come early; the queue forms fast.

places.ad: Jin Fa Kopitiam, Blk 24 Sin Ming Road, #01-51, S570024
places.w: On the Sin Ming edge of AMK, this corner stall traces back to a 1933 street-prata grandfather; the third generation flips 19 kinds and a famed hand-rolled Coin Prata set (S$4 for 6) that queues form for at breakfast.

places.ad: 237 Jalan Kayu, S799462
places.w: The stall that made 'Jalan Kayu prata' a Singapore byword — serving small, round, crispy prata (plus murtabak, mee goreng and biryani) since the 1960s, so copied that it signboards itself the 'Original Prata Shop'. Open 24 hours.

places.ad: Chong Boon Market & Food Centre, #01-01, Blk 453A Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560453
places.w: Around since 1957 and now third-generation, Rahim's Straits Times-featured 'Power' mee rebus layers savoury satay peanut sauce and spiced chicken over the usual gravy — long queues at this Chong Boon stall for mee rebus and mee soto.

places.ad: Mayflower Market & Food Centre, #01-39, Blk 162 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560162
places.w: Hawker Ah Ho learned the wok some 30 years ago at a famed Bukit Batok stall and now fries a leaning-wet Hokkien mee of yellow noodles and thin bee hoon in umami prawn stock — once named a top-10 Hokkien mee by Lianhe Wanbao.

places.n: Song Heng Fishball Minced Meat Noodle
places.ad: Ang Mo Kio 628 Market & Food Centre, #01-75, Blk 628 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560628
places.w: The longest queue at 628 with almost no publicity — a balanced chilli-vinegar dry mee pok with bouncy fishballs and a lightly sweet pork soup; fishballs regularly sell out by 11am. Closed Tuesdays.

places.ad: Ang Mo Kio 628 Market & Food Centre, Blk 628 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560628
places.w: Millennial hawker Max left a finance job in 2020 and, after training at Hock Heng, opened this long-queue stall; the Signature Seafood Noodle (from S$5) plays like bak chor mee but with seafood in place of pork.

places.ad: Food Loft Kopitiam, Ang Mo Kio Ave 8, Singapore
places.w: Two Gen-Z hawkers both named Jie fry one dish only — a wok-hei Hokkien mee on a wide stove that chars the noodles before the homemade prawn stock goes in, with fresh pork lard and house chilli. Hour-long queues since 2024.

places.ad: Blk 202 Ang Mo Kio Ave 3, #01-1690, S560202
places.w: A family zi char in a HDB coffeeshop since 2003, beloved for crunchy salted-egg prawns, pumpkin prawns, Dong Po pork belly and the usual chilli/salted-egg crabs — a reliable AMK feast spot.

places.ad: Ang Mo Kio, Singapore (coffeeshop zi char; block to verify)
places.w: An old-school Teochew zi char in AMK serving chilli crab and Teochew classics at neighbourhood prices — a longstanding local favourite for casual family dinners.

places.ad: Blk 202 Ang Mo Kio Ave 3, #01-1682, S560202
places.w: A retro void-deck cafe doing nett-price Western brunch — fried chicken and waffles (S$13.90), eggs benedict, fish and chips — with free-flow ice cream thrown in with every main.

places.ad: Teck Ghee Court Market & Food Centre, #01-04, Blk 341 Ang Mo Kio Ave 1, S560341
places.w: A lunchtime-queue fixture at Teck Ghee for peppery Singapore-style bak kut teh (S$8) and a fork-tender braised pig's trotter (S$7) in a dark, wine-scented lor bak gravy.

places.ad: Cheng San Market & Cooked Food Centre, Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, Singapore
places.w: Twenty years of Teochew-style porridge and a spread of 30-plus sides — fresh fish, fried meatballs, braised pork belly — one of Cheng San's most reliable old-school stalls.

places.ad: Cheng San Centre, Blk 532 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, #01-2495, S560532
places.w: One of few halal-certified fishball noodle stalls, a hotspot for the Malay community — large hand-scooped fishballs on a family recipe, around S$5.50-6.50. Moved to Cheng San/AMK from Upper Thomson in Dec 2022.

places.ad: Ang Mo Kio Central Market & Food Centre, #01-12, Blk 724 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, S560724
places.w: Thin rice vermicelli drowned in a thick, peanut-heavy satay sauce with cuttlefish, prawns, pork, tau pok and kang kong (from ~S$4) — rated by some as the best satay bee hoon around.

places.ad: Kebun Baru Market & Food Centre, #01-20, Blk 226H Ang Mo Kio Ave 1, S560226
places.w: Over four decades of herbal braised duck at Kebun Baru — the braise draws on more than ten herbs for a deep, aromatic gravy over rice or noodles.

places.ad: Sembawang Hills Food Centre, #01-04, 590 Upper Thomson Road, S574419
places.w: Sembawang Hills' standout fishball noodle — a dry mee pok tossed in a house blend of chilli, vinegar and tomato, with fishballs, fishcake and pork liver served in a light porky soup.

places.ad: Ang Mo Kio Central Market & Food Centre, Blk 724 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, S560724
places.w: A traditional Hainanese chicken rice counter that regularly makes the round-ups of 724 AMK Central's best — poached chicken and fragrant rice at heartland prices.

places.ad: Ang Mo Kio 628 Market & Food Centre, Blk 628 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560628
places.w: A 628 stall specialising in the trio of fried Hokkien prawn mee, fried carrot cake and oyster omelette — a solid all-rounder in one of AMK's most food-dense hawker centres.

places.n: Ang Mo Kio Loh Mee Laksa
places.ad: Chong Boon Market & Food Centre, #01-17, Blk 453A Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560453
places.w: An elderly couple has run this Chong Boon stall for more than a decade, doing two things well — a thick-gravy lor mee and a coconutty laksa.

places.ad: Chong Boon Market & Food Centre, #01-10, Blk 453A Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560453
places.w: Known at Chong Boon for an affordable, generous red grouper fish-head soup (around S$10) — a comforting, clean-tasting bowl.

places.ad: Chong Boon Market & Food Centre, #01-19, Blk 453A Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560453
places.w: A morning go-to at Chong Boon for silky, smooth poached chicken and fragrant rice.

places.ad: Chong Boon Market & Food Centre, #01-39, Blk 453A Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560453
places.w: A 12-year Chong Boon stall that draws one of the centre's longest queues for its dry-tossed noodles.

places.ad: Kebun Baru Market & Food Centre, #01-05, Blk 226H Ang Mo Kio Ave 1, S560226
places.w: A 31-year Kebun Baru stall serving a tidy small wanton noodle from S$3.50 — old-school springy mee and char siew.

places.n: Foo Hing Handmade Fishball & Meatball Noodle
places.ad: Kebun Baru Market & Food Centre, #01-01, Blk 226H Ang Mo Kio Ave 1, S560226
places.w: A Kebun Baru fixture for handmade fishballs and meatballs in a clean noodle bowl — one of the centre's most-recommended stalls.

places.ad: Blk 555 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, #01-1936, S560555
places.w: A no-frills 24-hour spot where every basket of dim sum is S$1.30 (buy 10, get 1 free) — fried prawn dumplings and siew mai the picks; not fine dining, but unbeatable value.

places.ad: Sembawang Hills Food Centre, 590 Upper Thomson Road, S574419
places.w: A perennial peak-hour queue at Sembawang Hills for a fresh sliced-fish seafood soup — ladle it over ke kou mian or bee hoon to soak up the broth.

places.ad: 16 Jalan Leban, Singapore 577554
places.w: Widely called Singapore's oldest Hakka restaurant (going back to 1960s Chin Swee Road, at Jalan Leban on the Sembawang Hills/AMK fringe for over 30 years) — the abacus seeds are pounded with more yam than flour and wok-fried with dried shrimp, minced pork and mushroom, alongside stuffed beancurd, khong bak and festive poon choi.

places.n: Xi Xiang Feng Yong Tau Foo
places.ad: Ang Mo Kio Central Market & Food Centre, #01-23, Blk 724 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, S560724
places.w: Reliably the longest queue at 724 AMK Central — a half-hour wait even off-peak — for a yong tau foo rated among the island's best, its handmade pieces defined by a deeply savoury house sauce; order it over chee cheong fun (S$0.80) or as laksa (S$3). Widely reviewed by ieatishootipost, Miss Tam Chiak, Eatbook and Seth Lui.

places.ad: 409 AMK Market & Food Centre, #01-15, Blk 409 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560409
places.w: A two-brother sliced-fish soup stall at 409 (Teck Ghee Square) whose broth balances savoury, sweet and a tang from fresh tomato, layered with tee po (dried sole), soy beans, tofu and seaweed. The queue runs 30 minutes even off-peak; soup from S$5.50, +S$0.50 with bee hoon.

places.ad: Blk 529 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, #01-2353, S560529
places.w: The heartland flagship of the North Bridge Road dessert cafe, doing waffle-and-ice-cream sets in an AMK void deck — the charcoal waffle with salted-egg drizzle (S$8.50), an AMK-exclusive 'Yuan Yang' half-charcoal-half-Belgian waffle, and a toasted-marshmallow S'mores waffle (S$15). Open late on weekends.

places.ad: 136-138 Casuarina Road, Singapore 579526
places.w: One of Singapore's most famous prata houses, on the Casuarina Road / Lower Peirce fringe of AMK — light, ghee-fragrant prata across 60-plus flavours (from Alfredo to salted-egg prawn), plus fish head curry, biryani, thosai and the off-menu R.K. Special (prata in mutton curry with soft-boiled eggs). Open till late.

places.ad: Cheng San Market & Cooked Food Centre, #01-123, Blk 527 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560527
places.w: Opened by one of the sisters from the original Song Kee, this Cheng San branch draws long queues (fishballs can sell out by 1pm) for honest handmade fishballs — bouncy, not over-salted — with an enhanced fishball and beancurd skin in each bowl. Closed Mondays.

places.ad: Blk 151 Ang Mo Kio Ave 5, #01-05, S560151
places.w: A long-running Kebun Bahru stall plating Thai-style wanton noodles — al dente egg noodles lightly coated in shallot oil, springy and eggy, with fried wanton, flavourful char siew and crisp pork lard. A dish rarely found outside Thailand and a longtime AMK draw.

places.ad: Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park, 510 Ang Mo Kio Ave 1, Singapore 569983
places.w: A family-friendly bistro set midway through Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park with an alfresco deck over the greenery — Asian-twist brunch of har cheong gai and waffles, truffled egg cocotte, mentaiko fries and a sustainable-fish crispy burger, with craft brews. Around S$22/pax; go early before the queue.

places.ad: Blk 260 Ang Mo Kio Street 21, #01-04, S560260
places.w: A hidden Vietnamese nook in a new AMK BTO estate — a crunchy, well-stuffed Saigon banh mi (S$6.90) with pork floss and meats, plus a milky, subtly savoury ice salted coffee (S$4.90). Small, cash-and-carry, and a genuine rarity in the heartland.

places.ad: Blk 347 Ang Mo Kio Ave 3, #01-2142, S560347
places.w: An old-school hawker-Western institution first opened in 1994 (originally at Blk 711 Ave 8) that reappeared at Blk 347 in 2021 to steady queues — thin, crispy chicken cutlet, pork chop, fish and chips and sirloin steak at heartland prices, in the Hainanese-Western tradition. Closed Wednesdays.

places.ad: Mayflower Market & Food Centre, #01-06, Blk 162 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560162
places.w: A humble Mayflower stall run by three sisters, doing a comforting prawn mee alongside fried Hokkien mee at value prices with generous prawns — friendly service and moderate waits. Opens from 6am; closed Wednesdays.

places.ad: Cheng San Market & Cooked Food Centre, #01-110, Blk 527 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560527
places.w: Founded in 1992 and run by a father and his two sons, this perpetually-queued Cheng San stall poaches its chicken the traditional way — an ice bath sets the gelatin under the skin for a slippery, slightly fatty finish — and debones it for you. Plates around S$4.50.

places.n: Seletar Sheng Mian & Mian Fen Guo
places.ad: Kebun Baru Market & Food Centre, #01-07, Blk 226H Ang Mo Kio Street 22, S560226
places.w: A perpetual-queue stall at Kebun Baru for hand-torn mee hoon kueh and hand-pulled sheng mian, the noodles the pride of the house, in a broth boiled with pork bones and ikan bilis for a natural sweetness. Dry or soup, S$4-6.

places.ad: Teck Ghee Court Market & Food Centre, #01-27, Blk 341 Ang Mo Kio Ave 1, S560341
places.w: Aunty Belinda's morning stall at Teck Ghee Court is prized for min jiang kueh with a generous filling-to-pancake ratio (peanut, coconut or red bean), a crisp cone-crepe version, and putu mayam (S$1.80 for two). Often sold out before noon.

places.ad: Sembawang Hills Food Centre, 590 Upper Thomson Road, S574419
places.w: A traditional kopi-and-toast stall serving breakfast since 1968, now run by a third-generation mother-and-son duo — award-winning homemade kaya with a strong coconut aroma slathered on soft, crisp-edged 'Emperor' buns, paired with sous-vide eggs and old-school kopi.

places.n: Hong Heng Beef Noodle Soup & Laksa
places.ad: Kebun Baru Market & Food Centre, #01-16, Blk 226H Ang Mo Kio Street 22, S560226
places.w: A rare stall selling both beef noodles and laksa under one roof — and, unusually, a Mixed Beef Laksa (S$5.50) that spoons coconut-rich laksa gravy over tender beef. Also a dry beef noodle with thick bee hoon and a fresh-cockles laksa. Relocated to Kebun Baru from AMK Ave 3; closed Mondays.

places.ad: Ang Mo Kio (void-deck cafe; exact block to confirm at geocode)
places.w: A cosy void-deck cafe (Fried Ice Cream) that pairs its signature fried ice cream with Vietnamese-leaning bites — an unpretentious neighbourhood dessert-and-coffee spot that made both Eatbook's and HungryGoWhere's Ang Mo Kio round-ups.

places.ad: Mayflower Market & Food Centre, Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560162 (stall no. to confirm)
places.w: A value-for-money wanton mee whose secret is in the lard-based sauce — springy egg noodles loaded with braised chicken feet, char siew and crispy pork lard bits. A long-standing local favourite carried over from its Blk 453 origins.

places.ad: Chengsan Centre, #01-2371, Blk 529 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560529
places.w: A homely Thai stall (also in Toa Payoh) plating authentic street-Thai — a prawn-generous seafood tom yum nam kun (S$6.50), green curry with prawns, papaya salad and a peppery claypot tanghoon with prawns that stays springy. Affordable and consistently recommended.

places.ad: Blk 716 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, #01-4014, S560716
places.w: A quiet void-deck specialty-coffee cafe on AMK Ave 6 — espresso and pour-overs with cakes and light bites, one of the heartland cafe finds featured in both Daniel Food Diary's and HungryGoWhere's Ang Mo Kio guides.

places.ad: Ang Mo Kio Central Market & Food Centre, #01-39, Blk 724 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, S560724
places.w: A Michelin Guide-listed old-school minced meat noodle at 724 AMK Central — springy mee pok or mee kia tossed in a distinctive ketchup-forward chilli sauce with minced pork, braised mushroom and a round cracker, from S$3. Loaded portions and one of the heartland's most-cited bak chor mee stalls.

places.n: Eng Ho Fried Hokkien Prawn Mee
places.ad: 409 AMK Market & Food Centre (Teck Ghee Square), #01-34, Blk 409 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560409
places.w: A wetter, prawn-stock-drenched fried Hokkien mee at 409 (Teck Ghee Square) built on a rich stock of wild sea prawns (swa lor), squid and pork for a sweeter, more delicate depth. Fried in batches with 30-40 minute peak-hour waits; named a top-10 Hokkien mee in Singapore by Lianhe Wanbao. Opens 4pm, closed alternate Tuesdays.

places.n: Zhen Ming Pork Ribs Prawn Noodle
places.ad: Mayflower Market & Food Centre, #01-04, Blk 162 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560162
places.w: A 20-plus-year Mayflower stall whose brown prawn broth is simmered at least six hours with pork ribs, pig skin, red dates, prawn shells and black sugarcane (in place of rock sugar) for a natural, addictive sweetness — served dry or soup with fishcake, lean meat, Brazilian pork ribs and prawns. Mornings only; closed Tuesdays.

places.ad: Kebun Baru Market & Food Centre, Blk 226H Ang Mo Kio Street 22, S560226 (stall no. to confirm)
places.w: A perpetual pre-lunch queue at Kebun Baru since Dec 2020 for a Johor-Bahru-style bi tai mak (S$4) rarely found this side of the Causeway — freshly-made 'rat-tail' noodles in a viscous, gravy-like broth crossing robust pork stock with light ikan bilis, studded with minced pork, mushroom, hae bee, garlic, fried shallots and salted fish. Sells out before lunch.

places.ad: 258 Jalan Kayu, S799487
places.w: A 24-hour Jalan Kayu institution on the AMK/Seletar fringe serving Singaporean, Malay, Thai and South Indian fare — famed for its prata, biryani, satay and curry fish head, with an air-conditioned wing alongside the coffeeshop seating. Packed at breakfast and supper.

places.ad: Sembawang Hills Food Centre, #01-32, 590 Upper Thomson Road, S574419
places.w: A Sembawang Hills favourite (formerly at Shunfu/Lakeview) for a wet, wok-hei char kway teow with cockles, beansprouts and Chinese sausage from S$3, best paired with its smoky S$1 otah. Closed Mondays.

places.ad: Blk 260 Ang Mo Kio Street 21, S560260
places.w: A Muslim-owned dim sum stall (sharing a coffeeshop with Friends Kitchen HK, whose team co-owns it) doing an unusually wide handmade range from S$2.50 — chunky chicken-and-shrimp siew mai, fluffy BBQ chicken buns and salted-egg lava buns — a genuine rarity as halal dim sum in the heartland.

places.ad: Blk 163 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, #01-414, S560163
places.w: A 2025-opened old-school Nanyang cafe doing classic heartland fare — mani cai (sayur manis) mee hoon kueh, laksa, steamed toast and frothy kopi, most mains under S$8, CDC vouchers accepted. Open daily 7am-10pm.

places.ad: Blk 128 Ang Mo Kio Ave 3, #01-1867, S560128
places.w: A void-deck gelato cafe themed around mahjong — flavours inspired by Chinese sweets, served with Belgian waffles, croffles and pandan-mochi or nian gao waffles, the tiles motif carried playfully through the shop. Open till late on weekends.

places.ad: Ang Mo Kio 628 Market & Food Centre, #01-97, Blk 628 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560628
places.w: A home-style Malay stall at 628 turning out comforting mee soto, mee rebus, lontong and nasi lemak — a neighbourhood staple recommended in both Seth Lui's and Eatbook's 628 round-ups.

places.ad: Ang Mo Kio 628 Market & Food Centre, #01-70, Blk 628 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560628
places.w: A 628 vegetarian stall doing curry vegetarian bee hoon in the morning and, from mid-afternoon, meat-free zi char — mock duck rice, fish-soup bee hoon and stir-fried sweet potato leaves — a rare all-vegetarian option in the centre.

places.ad: Sembawang Hills Food Centre, #01-27, 590 Upper Thomson Road, S574419
places.w: A long-loved, no-frills braised duck rice and porridge counter at Sembawang Hills, a Thomson-and-Sembawang neighbourhood standby featured across the centre's guides.

places.ad: Sembawang Hills Food Centre, #01-17, 590 Upper Thomson Road, S574419
places.w: A Muslim-owned, halal-certified stall at Sembawang Hills known for a rich, gooey mee rebus alongside mee siam, lontong and nasi lemak — homely Malay breakfast fare in a mostly-Chinese food centre.

places.n: Xiang Kee Yu Yuan Mian Tang
places.ad: Cheng San Market & Cooked Food Centre, #01-125, Blk 527 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560527
places.w: A husband-and-wife fishball noodle stall of some 30 years at Cheng San — a lardy, savoury-tangy fishball kway teow soup (from S$4) with minced meat, mushroom, pork lard and fresh liver, its in-house chilli of dried chillies and shallots giving a fiery kick. Queues form from 7am; closed Mondays.

places.ad: Ang Mo Kio Central Market & Food Centre, #01-08, Blk 724 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, S560724
places.w: A 724 AMK Central Western stall going since the 1990s, a longstanding heartland pick for grilled and deep-fried meats — chicken, pork chop and steak — in the old-school Hainanese-Western tradition. Opens afternoons, closed Mondays.

places.ad: Blk 446 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, #01-1661, S560446
places.w: An under-HDB dessert cafe doing chewy mochi pancakes, mochi waffles and gelato at nett prices (from S$4.50), open late on weekends — a 14-minute walk from AMK MRT. (Status to re-verify: one report suggests the unit has since changed hands.)
